subject: general
question: In a lathe with a 3-jaw chuck, how are the jaws moved?

options.text: By rotating the pinion simultaneously in a radial direction

solution:
**Concept**

 
• A 3-jaw chuck is also known as a self-centering chuck or a universal chuck.
 
• It is designed to hold hexagonal or cylindrical workpieces centrally with respect to the lathe axis.
 
• The primary characteristic of this chuck is that all three jaws move simultaneously when any one of the pinion sockets is rotated.

**Explanation**

The internal mechanism of a 3-jaw chuck consists of two main parts: the scroll plate and the bevel pinions.

1. **Scroll Plate:** This is a circular plate that has a spiral groove (scroll) on its front face and bevel teeth on its back
